changeability.rationale: The headline bug lands in one obvious place thanks to the api/format seam, but the three-fold duplication of ref-to-species card-list assembly means the next behaviour change in that rule (form exclusion, dedupe, hidden-ability merge) lands in three pages, not one.

app/components/MovesSection.tsx:3 — 'use client' boundaries are minimal (HomeBrowser, MovesSection) and receive plain serialized data from server pages

coupling.rationale: Loose coupling overall: one data module, narrow component interfaces, clean server/client split. Only mild tangles — a client component that knows the pokemon route shape, two different URL-sync idioms, and badge markup that bypasses the existing component.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:16 — good small primitives: cached()/apiFetch pattern, frontSpriteUrl/assetUrl, format.ts helpers; adding getItem follows the same pattern
app/app/moves/[name]/page.tsx:39-57 — 'Pokémon card list from resource refs' appears 3x server-side + HomeBrowser with no shared abstraction, so sorting/pagination variants are N-copy changes
app/components/PokemonCard.tsx:1 — the card itself is well-factored and reused by all four lists
abstraction_design.rationale: The primitives are right-sized and reused, but the app's real recurring shape — a species card list — was never abstracted, so each similar list is a fresh copy of ~20 lines of resolution logic. No flag-parameter creep, though, and MovesSection nicely separates data prep (server) from sorting (client).

findings.issue: Species-resolution + card-list assembly (speciesById map, form exclusion, dedupe, dex sort, count line, ul.card-grid) is duplicated across moves, abilities and types pages
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared helper/component, e.g. lib/species.ts resolveSpeciesList(refs) plus a PokemonCardList component; name-sorting (scenario 3) and form-rule changes then become one edit

findings.issue: dynamic='force-dynamic' + revalidate=0 (+ fetchCache) repeated in 8 segment files; redundant on pages that already read params/searchParams, and the Next 16 direction (cacheComponents/use cache) replaces these configs plus the custom cached() Map in lib/api.ts:16
findings.suggestion: Declare it once in the root layout, or drop it where dynamic params already force dynamic rendering, and note the lib/api.ts cached() Map is the thing to migrate to 'use cache' when adopting the current model

findings.issue: Two different URL-sync mechanisms: window.history.replaceState in HomeBrowser vs router.replace in MovesSection.tsx:83
findings.suggestion: Standardize on one approach (the history.replaceState trick is defensible to avoid a server round-trip, but document it or wrap it in a small useQuerySync hook)

findings.issue: TypeBadge component is bypassed: raw `type-badge type-X` Link markup is hand-rolled here, in moves/[name]/page.tsx:79 and MovesSection.tsx:160
findings.suggestion: Route all type badges through TypeBadge (extend it with className if needed) so the badge markup and class naming live in one file

findings.issue: getEnglishMoveName is exported but never used (dead code)
findings.suggestion: Delete it; callers use englishName(move.names, ...) directly

findings.issue: first() searchParams-normalization helper duplicated in app/pokemon/[name]/page.tsx:38
findings.suggestion: Move to lib/format.ts (or a small lib/search-params.ts) and import in both

findings.issue: Client component hardcodes the /pokemon/<slug> route shape, coupling it to the pokemon page's URL convention
findings.suggestion: Pass a prebuilt gameHref pattern or base path as a prop, or centralize route builders in lib/format.ts

summary: This is a tidy, well-seamed codebase: all API access and formatting rules are centralized, components are small and props-driven, and the server/client split is deliberate. Its main editability debt is that 'a list of Pokémon cards from resource references' — the app's most repeated shape — is copy-pasted across three server pages plus the home browser, so anything touching that rule (sorting, form exclusion, pagination) is a multi-file change. The redundant per-segment caching directives across 8 files are minor but worth consolidating given Next 16's move to use cache.
